people.name: Hugh Barlow
notes: Research 24 Sep 2026. This is currently the end of the documented Barlow line: Hugh Barlow has no sourced birth/christening record and no parents recorded in FamilySearch Family Tree.
Children recorded: Francis (1638/9, our line) and Sammuell (1649/50) -- both sourced. 'Frances' (1639) is a likely duplicate of Francis, not a real third child -- see the family element.
Mucklestone is a Staffordshire village near the Cheshire border, roughly midway between Barlow, Derbyshire and the Barlow manor near Manchester, Lancashire.

William Barlow of Mucklestone (m. Anne, gedcom I900109) is treated as the same person as William Barlow baptised 1606 at Betley, son of Ranulph. Hugh may still be a kinsman of that family (e.g. a cousin), but no record shows it.

Leads checked and ruled out (24 Sep 2026): a 'Hugh Barlow' buried 1668 at Mucklestone (attached by FamilySearch to a younger Hugh, b.1638); a Norton-in-the-Moors Hugh cluster (too late); George Barlow (bapt.1595/6, Betley, son of Roger Barlow, not Ranulph); a Biddulph Barlow family (separate).
24 Sep 2026, exhaustive FreeREG pass across Mucklestone, Betley, Staffordshire, Cheshire and Shropshire (exact and fuzzy): no baptism or marriage for Hugh Barlow x Elizabeth found.

13 Oct 2026: RANULPH HYPOTHESIS RULED OUT. Ranulph (Randull) Barlow's will (dated 3 Feb 1639/40, proved 5 Mar 1639/40, Staffordshire Record Office B/C/11) was read from images. It names five children, each given the 12d 'child's part or filial portion' formula meant to cover all children: Roger, William, Elizabeth, Dorothy and Margery. Hugh, alive at the time, is not among them. The hypothesis child edge from Ranulph's family has been removed.

Remaining avenues: Mucklestone original registers or bishop's transcripts for c.1600-1620 (Staffordshire Record Office); Hugh's marriage to Elizabeth (c.1635-1638) in surrounding parishes; Y-DNA against a Barlow surname project.

leads.body: They came in with the original family tree file and nothing has been attached since. These are the cheapest wins: one record each.

leads.title: 30 people have no dates at all
leads.body: They are placed on the river by estimating from parents, partners and children, and drawn with a dashed ring. Any one baptism or burial would pin a whole family down.

facts.title: The river reaches New Zealand in 1855
facts.body: George Creighton Finch is the first person in the tree recorded as born in New Zealand, in Howick Auckland NZ. A parent was born in Suffolk. Switch to the place lens and play from 1800 to watch the colour change.

facts.title: The oldest dated record is from 1592
facts.body: Elizabeth Barlow, born 10 Nov 1592 at Betley. Everything earlier in the tree is an estimate.

facts.title: 14 children in one family
facts.body: Peter Seaman and Anne Meachen have the most children recorded of any couple in the tree.

facts.title: Miriam Carter lived to 104
facts.body: Born 1871, died 1975. The longest life in the tree with both dates on record.

facts.title: 11 children did not reach six
facts.body: These are the ones with both dates recorded. 5 were born before 1800. The real number is higher: children who died young are the people most often missing from a tree.

facts.title: 26 people are called Elizabeth
facts.body: The most used first names in the tree are Elizabeth (26), William (19), Mary (17).

facts.title: 14% of people cite a record
facts.body: Of 340 people shown, 48 cite a parish register, will, census or similar. 191 rest only on someone else's tree. 101 cite nothing. Switch to the certainty lens to see where each kind sits.
